items.title: ‘I can’t die like this’: flydubai pilot recounts ordeal of cockpit attack
items.description: The captain of a flydubai flight whose co-pilot attacked him with an axe in an alleged bid to bring down the plane said one thought kept running through his head as the harrowing ordeal unfolded: “You can’t die like this.” Read Also: ‘I could not let all those people die’ — Indian pilot recounts flydubai ordeal Indian pilot Smit Machchhar recounted the “traumatic” experience to Sky News Arabia in his first interview since the incident late last month in which he, passengers and other crew members were credited with averting disaster on the Tel Aviv-bound flight. With his head and one hand bandaged and glasses perched on his nose, Machchhar spoke from his hospital bed in the UAE. “My vision was restricted to a few inches,” said the pilot, describing the effect of being struck in the back of the head with an emergency axe by his co-pilot, who had positioned himself behind Machchhar’s seat. At first thinking that a part of the airplane’s ceiling had come loose, he then received several more blows and was wounded in the hand as he tried to shield himself. Machchhar recalled struggling to open the cockpit door so another pilot who was travelling on board could get inside. “So I was screaming his name and I was trying, because the switch that was very close to me to open the door, I was trying to just get help in,” he said. “But I remember being able to open the door,” he went on, only for it to shut again. “And at that point, I felt all the blood, you know, everything rushing down, my energy, everything, I was just, I was barely staying in consciousness.” “Soon after that, that was the time when I heard the engine sounds going down. And then immediately after that I felt the aircraft going into a dive.” According to findings released by the Emirati attorney general, Machchhar’s 29-year-old Omani co-pilot had planned to use the plane to carry out a suicide attack on the passenger terminal at Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv, inspired by the September 11, 2001 attacks in New York. He claimed to have acted alone, something investigators are still working to verify. The prosecutor found that the other pilot on board, having seen the cockpit door open and close “in an unusual manner”, entered the flight deck and with the help of another crew member and passengers, subdued the co-pilot and regained control of the aircraft. The jet, which plunged violently during the fray, was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Machchhar said the way his colleague was able to intervene and safely land the plane was “commendable”. “It’s something that I’ll keep with me till I die.” The post ‘I can’t die like this’: flydubai pilot recounts ordeal of cockpit attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: France : 550.000 manifestants en France dont 110.000 à Paris
items.description: Environ 550.000 personnes ont manifesté samedi en France, dont 110.000 à Paris, lors de la journée de mobilisation contre la « vie chère » et environ 400 personnes, « en majorité des majeurs » , ont été interpellées, a annoncé le ministre de l'Intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, qui a pointé la responsabilité « l'ultragauche » dans les actions violentes. S'exprimant devant la presse, qui a dénombré 110 défilés samedi, Nuñez a fait valoir qu'en marge des cortèges, s'étaient constitués « des groupes de casseurs – plusieurs centaines, plusieurs milliers parfois selon les lieux – à l'instigation très claire de l'ultragauche ». Il a également souligné que des « délinquants d'opportunité » en avaient profité « pour s'en prendre à des commerces » et les « piller ». Cellule de crise à Matignon De son côté, le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu préside samedi soir la cellule interministérielle de crise, mise en place plus tôt dans la journée, pour faire le point sur les violences qui se prolongent après les manifestations du 17 octobre, à fait savoir Matignon. Seront notamment présents autour de lui le ministre de la Justice, Gérald Darmanin et son collègue de l'Intérieur, Laurent Nuñez. items.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe Unknown gunmen have killed two policemen and burnt buildings and a patrol van at the Uratta Police Division, in Aba, Abia State. Confirming the incident, Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) of the Command, DSP Maureen Chinaka, disclosed that the hoodlums attacked the division with explosives, resulting in a fire that damaged part of the building and the divisional patrol van. She added that two police officers lost their lives, while three inspectors sustained injuries and are currently receiving medical attention. The Command further clarified that no firearms or ammunition were carted away by the attackers during the incident. The PPRO explained that the Commissioner of Police, Abia State Command, CP Wilfred Afolabi, had personally led an operational team to the area. She also stated that the team combed the surrounding environment and restored calm, while intensified security operations and monitoring are ongoing to apprehend the hoodlums. The PPRO assured that the Command will deploy all necessary operational and intelligence resources to identify and apprehend those responsible, assuring that the hoodlums will be brought to justice. “The Command extends its heartfelt condolences to the families of the fallen officers and the entire Police family over this painful loss. “Residents are urged to remain calm, vigilant and to support the Police with credible information that could assist the ongoing investigation. “Information can be reported at the nearest police station, through the suggestion boxes and contact details of the DPO’s provided at police divisions, or via the Command’s emergency hotlines: 08035415405,08079210004, 08079210005, 08079210006.” Vanguard gathered that Governor Alex Otti had visited the police station as well as the injured policemen at the hospital. items.title: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats, beat French mayor
items.description: Israeli settlers on Saturday attacked a convoy of European diplomats and beat up a visiting French mayor, in a new escalation of violence during the Palestinian olive harvest, witnesses and diplomats told AFP. The 78-year-old mayor said masked settlers yelled defamatory comments about France, kicked him and hit him with iron bars as he joined Palestinian olive farmers in the West Bank alongside the top French and Belgian representatives in Jerusalem and Polish diplomats. “I think that if settlers are behaving like this, there is a tolerance on the part of the Israeli government,” Bernard Baudoux, mayor of the northern French town of Aulnoye-Aymeries, told AFP after he was attacked. “The whole world needs to know what’s happening,” he said. “For me, I’ll go back to my country and everything will be fine. Those who continue to suffer the most are those who are here.” Baudoux, who was wearing a sash with the French tricolour, was seen collapsed on the side of the car after the attack but he did not need hospital care. The attack came just one day after settlers beat an American photographer for The Washington Post, who was in moderate condition with broken vertebrae on Saturday. Israel’s foreign ministry condemned the attack on the diplomats and Israeli police promised to open an investigation. But Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, days away from an election in which he is seeking to shore up support from the far-right, instead alleged a “smear” campaign against settlers. Netanyahu said the diplomats should have coordinated their movements with the Israeli military and pointed out that Baudoux is a communist known for supporting the Palestinian cause. “We urge caution before drawing conclusions” about the attacks, Netanyahu’s office said in a statement. His main rival in October 27 elections, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, strongly criticised Netanyahu over the violence, saying it was “burning away the little legitimacy the State of Israel still possesses”. The attacks are “Jewish terrorism, under the auspices of the Israeli government”, Eisenkot said. Belgium called for an end to “impunity for violent settlers” after the latest attack. Attacks on cultural symbol Baudoux, the mayor, said he had come to the town of Taybeh, a Christian stronghold, along with his local pastor from France to sign a goodwill agreement. He was attacked just as he joined the harvest as a symbolic gesture with the Palestinians, for whom olives are an important cultural symbol. Extremist Israelis have issued calls to stop the Palestinians’ harvest after months of growing attacks in which settlers have stolen land and property. There has also been violence against Israelis, with a Palestinian shooting dead a settler last month. Bashar Fawadleh, a priest in Taybeh, said settlers had already attacked the harvest and snatched olives before beating the mayor. “One person was hit in the head and needed stitches. They also beat up an older lady in her 70s after insulting her with very bad words,” the pastor told AFP. The West Bank violence has shocked much of the world, with Britain leading economic sanctions that in turn caused Netanyahu to voice outrage. Netanyahu had also sought to throw doubt on the circumstances behind the beating Friday of the photographer, Heidi Levine, suggesting that Palestinians and “far-left” activists caused trouble. But President Isaac Herzog, who holds a mostly symbolic role, took the initiative Saturday to call Levine in the hospital, calling the attack “outrageous and shocking” and saying it weighed on his conscience. Israel Gantz, head of an umbrella settler group, blamed the recent incidents on “groups of provocateurs and terrorists” and implicitly acknowledged some Israelis’ responsibility, saying that they caused harm to the settlers’ cause. Settlers earlier this month also beat up AFP photographer Jaafar Ashtiyeh as he covered the olive harvest tensions, fracturing several of his ribs. Netanyahu’s government has ramped up approval of West Bank settlements, which are illegal under international law. Some 500,000 Israelis live in the West Bank, which Israel seized in 1967, alongside three million Palestinians. items.title: Labé : candidats et autorités confiants au concours de recrutement des enseignants
items.description: Le concours de recrutement des enseignants a mobilisé, ce samedi 17 octobre 2026, de nombreux candidats dans la région administrative de Labé. Au total, 3 183 candidats sont attendus dans cinq centres d’examen pour l’enseignement général et secondaire. Entre espoir d’intégrer la fonction publique, volonté de servir la nation et préoccupations liées au manque d’enseignants dans certaines localités, les candidats abordent les épreuves avec détermination. De leur côté, les autorités assurent que toutes les dispositions sont prises pour garantir le bon déroulement du concours et mettent en avant des innovations numériques destinées à accélérer la correction et le classement. Superviseur du concours à Labé, Yamoussa Nana Camara, conseiller juridique du ministre de la Modernisation de l’administration et de la Fonction publique, a souligné l’importance de ce recrutement pour le renforcement des capacités de l’administration guinéenne, notamment dans le secteur de l’éducation. « Ce recrutement s’inscrit dans le cadre du renforcement des capacités de l’ensemble de l’administration. Chacun de nous réclame aujourd’hui un bon enseignement dans notre système éducatif. Pour avoir un bon enseignement, il faut recruter des enseignants et il faut les former », a-t-il expliqué. Selon lui, la région administrative de Labé compte 3 183 candidats pour l’enseignement général et secondaire, répartis dans cinq centres d’examen. Il a également rappelé les consignes à respecter, notamment l’interdiction d’introduire des téléphones portables ou tout autre objet non autorisé dans les salles d’examen. Le superviseur a par ailleurs insisté sur les innovations numériques introduites dans le processus de correction et de classement des candidats. « Nous avons apporté beaucoup d’innovations au niveau du numérique. C’est la machine qui fait la correction et le classement. Le jury ne se réunit que pour valider. C’est un travail qui sera fait dans les brefs délais », a-t-il précisé. Il estime ainsi que les résultats pourraient être disponibles rapidement, éventuellement dès le lendemain ou dans les deux jours suivant les épreuves. Du côté des candidats, l’espoir et la détermination dominent. Venu de Conakry pour tenter sa chance, Mohammed Lamine Bangoura affirme aborder les épreuves avec un bon état d’esprit. « Le moral est là et j’espère que ça va bien se passer. J’ai postulé parce que c’est le seul moyen de servir ma nation », a-t-il déclaré. Candidat à l’enseignement général, il a choisi la préfecture de Tougué comme destination. Même détermination chez Bah Mamadou Lamine, enseignant à l’école primaire de Saala, qui participe au concours dans l’espoir de saisir une nouvelle opportunité professionnelle. Il se réjouit de l’engouement suscité par cette opération de recrutement. « Je suis là aujourd’hui pour essayer de tenter ma chance. On est très heureux de voir un engouement très grand », a-t-il confié. Pour Barry Hadjiratou, également candidate à l’enseignement général dans la préfecture de Tougué, ce concours représente une occasion d’intégrer la fonction publique et de poursuivre son engagement dans l’éducation. Contractuelle en situation de classe à Tougué, elle espère voir ses efforts récompensés. « Je suis motivée pour servir mon pays. Je prie le Bon Dieu qu’il me donne la chance d’intégrer la fonction publique », a-t-elle indiqué. De son côté, Baldé Mariam, qui travaille dans l’enseignement depuis 2023 à Tougué, dit aborder les épreuves avec sérénité. Elle espère réussir le concours, mais aussi contribuer à répondre aux besoins en personnel enseignant dans sa préfecture de travail. « Je suis venue avec un esprit très tranquille pour faire le concours et on souhaite avoir ce qu’on est venu chercher », a-t-elle expliqué, avant d’évoquer les difficultés liées au manque d’enseignants dans sa zone de travail. « Ce qui m’a motivée, premièrement, c’est le manque d’enseignants à Tougué. Nous espérons qu’il y aura beaucoup d’enseignants cette année à Tougué pour éviter que les enfants restent sans cours », a-t-elle ajouté. À travers ce concours, les autorités ambitionnent de renforcer les effectifs de l’administration publique et de répondre aux besoins du système éducatif. Pour les candidats, notamment ceux qui exercent déjà comme contractuels, l’enjeu est majeur : intégrer la fonction publique et contribuer à améliorer l’offre éducative dans les localités confrontées à un manque d’enseignants. Alpha Moussa Dieng, correspondant régional à Labé L’article Labé : candidats et autorités confiants au concours de recrutement des enseignants est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Le Maroc lance les appels d'offre pour la construction de 11 barrages
items.description: La Direction des aménagements hydrauliques a lancé 11 appels d'offre pour la construction de barrages répartis dans plusieurs provinces du Royaume. Cette opération majeure représente une enveloppe budgétaire prévisionnelle globale dépassant 339 millions de dirhams. Selon les données des marchés publics, ces chantiers structurants s'implanteront à travers huit provinces, à savoir Rehamna, Boulemane, Chefchaouen, Khouribga, Taroudant, Taourirt, Figuig et Zagora. Les projets nécessitant les investissements les plus conséquents concernent le barrage Ourir dans la province de Taroudant, estimé à près de 46,45 millions de dirhams, ainsi que le barrage Taghzout dans la province de Chefchaouen, dont le coût prévisionnel avoisine 46,22 millions de dirhams. Parmi les autres ouvrages programmés figurent ceux de Aglemam, dit Sidi Rabeh Ettolba, dans la province de Taourirt pour un montant d'environ 40,11 millions de dirhams, et de Hyara dans la province de Zagora pour un budget de 39,64 millions de dirhams. L'administration a également fixé le coût prévisionnel du barrage Agdim, dans la province de Boulemane, à près de 29,27 millions de dirhams, tandis que le barrage Dar Wa Thanaya dans la province de Rehamna est évalué à environ 29 millions de dirhams. Le programme englobe aussi les barrages Sidi Saïd et Oulad Sidi Daoud à Rehamna, Srirou à Khouribga, Aïssa Ben Omar à Taourirt et Ras Kraa à Figuig. Conformément au calendrier fixé par le ministère de tutelle, les séances d'ouverture des plis pour l'attribution des différents marchés se dérouleront entre le 9 et le 16 novembre 2026. items.title: Santé : Youns Bjijou prône l'intelligence collective pour répondre aux attentes des citoyens
items.description: La cérémonie de passation des pouvoirs entre Youns Bjijou, que le Roi Mohammed VI a nommé ministre de la Santé et de la Protection sociale, et Amine Tehraoui, s'est déroulée samedi à Rabat. A cette occasion, Bjijou a exprimé sa fierté de la Haute confiance royale placée en lui, s'engageant à mobiliser tous ses efforts pour être à la hauteur de cette responsabilité. Le ministre a mis en avant l'intérêt accordé au secteur de la santé et de la protection sociale, dans le sillage du Chantier Royal de généralisation de la protection sociale, notamment en ce qui concerne l'Assurance maladie obligatoire. Rappelant la réforme et la restructuration en cours dans ce secteur, il a affirmé que la prochaine étape exige d'œuvrer dans un esprit de concertation et d'intelligence collective pour répondre aux attentes des citoyens. Youns Bjijou a, dans ce sens, affirmé que l'objectif est désormais de renforcer la souveraineté sanitaire, de mettre à niveau les infrastructures, d'améliorer la gouvernance et d'investir dans le capital humain, en plus de l'accélération de la transformation numérique et de la gestion des données. Il a, par la même occasion, appelé l'ensemble des cadres et fonctionnaires du secteur à œuvrer de concert en vue de relever les défis et d'atteindre les objectifs de ce chantier stratégique majeur. Pour sa part, Amine Tehraoui a exprimé ses vives félicitations au nouveau ministre, lui souhaitant plein succès dans l'exercice de ses nouvelles fonctions. © Mounir Mehimdate Il a, également, rappelé les réalisations et les réformes importantes accomplies durant les dernières années, grâce au dévouement et au travail collectif des cadres et fonctionnaires du ministère. La gestion du secteur de la santé et de la protection sociale constitue une noble responsabilité, dont la finalité ultime est d'assurer des services de santé à l'ensemble des citoyens, a-t-il conclu. The post Santé : Youns Bjijou prône l'intelligence collective pour répondre aux attentes des citoyens appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Guinée : la route Labé–Tougué–Bafing–Koubia au cœur des travaux parlementaires en inter-commission
items.description: Dans le cadre de mes activités parlementaires au sein de la 10ᵉ législature de l’Assemblée nationale, j’ai pris part, ce jour, aux travaux en inter-commission consacrés à l’examen de la convention de crédit relative à la construction et au bitumage de la route Labé – Tougué – Bafing – Koubia, en présence des cadres des départements en charge des Finances, de l’Économie, des Infrastructures et des Travaux publics, ainsi que des Honorables députés. En ma qualité de membre de la Commission Commerce, Tourisme, Hôtellerie et Artisanat, j’ai particulièrement insisté sur les retombées économiques et sociales attendues de cette infrastructure stratégique pour la Moyenne-Guinée et pour l’ensemble de notre pays. Au-delà de la construction d’une route, ce projet représente une opportunité majeure pour faciliter la circulation des personnes et des biens, améliorer l’accès aux marchés, soutenir nos producteurs agricoles et nos éleveurs, réduire les coûts de transport et favoriser le développement des activités commerciales. Cependant, notre responsabilité parlementaire ne consiste pas uniquement à examiner les conditions de financement d’un projet. Elle consiste également à veiller à ce que les ressources mobilisées produisent des résultats concrets, durables et bénéfiques pour les populations. Au cours de nos travaux, j’ai tenu à mettre l’accent sur plusieurs exigences essentielles : Une concurrence loyale et transparente entre les entreprises nationales et internationales dans l’attribution des marchés publics ; La qualité et la durabilité des infrastructures, à travers des contrôles techniques rigoureux, des essais en laboratoire et le respect des normes de construction ; La protection des ressources publiques, par la maîtrise des coûts, la prévention des surfacturations, des conflits d’intérêts et des malfaçons ; La promotion du contenu local, en favorisant l’accès des PME guinéennes, des jeunes entrepreneurs, des entreprises dirigées par des femmes et des prestataires locaux aux opportunités générées par le projet ; La mise en place d’un mécanisme de suivi des retombées économiques, notamment en matière d’emplois, de sous-traitance, de commerce, de transport et d’écoulement des productions locales. Je demeure convaincu que la promotion des champions nationaux est indispensable à notre développement économique. Toutefois, elle doit s’accompagner d’exigences strictes de compétence, de transparence, de performance et de qualité. La préférence nationale ne doit jamais se faire au détriment de l’intérêt général, ni de la sécurité et du bien-être des citoyens. Notre priorité doit être claire : construire des infrastructures de qualité, protéger les deniers publics et garantir aux populations des routes durables, capables de soutenir véritablement le développement de nos territoires. Le désenclavement du Fouta n’est pas seulement une question de mobilité. C’est aussi un levier de croissance, de création d’emplois, de dynamisation du commerce et d’amélioration des conditions de vie de nos concitoyens. En tant que député national, je continuerai à défendre une approche responsable des investissements publics, fondée sur la transparence, la rigueur et la recherche permanente de résultats concrets pour le peuple guinéen. items.title: APC’s internal contradictions scare me more than Atiku, Obi – Shettima
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Vice President Kashim Shettima has said he fears divisions within the ruling All Progressives Congress APC more than he fears the opposition ahead of the 2027 general elections. Shettima spoke on Saturday in Abuja when he unveiled the campaign head office of Arewa for Asiwaju (A4A), a northern coalition backing the Tinubu/Shettima ticket, and formally inaugurated its campaign structure. “Honestly, I am not afraid of the Peoples Democratic Party PDP. I am not afraid of a diminished Peter Obi. But I am more afraid of internal contradictions within our household. If we unite as a people, as a family, we will conquer,” he said. He warned northern leaders against pursuing the presidential race at the expense of their governors. “There is no point in championing the cause of the presidential election and then undermining the governor in the gubernatorial election. Honestly, it will not go down well with the system,” he said. “Let’s rally round our governors. Let’s rally round our members of the National Assembly. Let’s rally round President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and see to the victory in the next round of elections,” he added. The Vice President said the North had already made its choice. “By now, I believe the North has spoken. We have spoken with a resounding voice and unmistakable conviction. From Adamawa to Zamfara, from Borno to Niger, we have spoken,” he said. He told the gathering that the poll is close. “In less than 100 days, Nigerians will return to the polls. Democracy requires us to seek their confidence again, with humility about the work outstanding and conviction about the cause we have chosen,” he said. On Atiku Abubakar, Shettima urged party members to take him on respectfully. “Go and perform. Go and defeat Baba Atiku. Defeat him respectfully,” he said. He said the party had the structure to contest every polling unit. “There are 176,845 polling units across the country. The APC, from ward to local government levels, has 361,045 officials. What it means is that we can match every polling unit two to two,” he said. Shettima said appointees must prove their local strength. “Politics is still local,” he said, adding that he had asked the Borno State governor to compile a list of all political appointees from the state to local government level. “Let him account for his performance at his polling unit, at his ward unit and in his local government,” he said. On the party’s standing in the North, he said, “Out of 19 states in the North, 18 are in the APC.” He said 15 of the 18 members of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) from Kano in the House of Representatives have crossed to the APC, adding: “The governor is with the APC.” The Vice President acknowledged that many families are struggling. “Every household struggling to make ends meet reminds us how much remains to be done,” he said. “We lose our hearing when applause becomes our only source of information.” Defending the administration’s economic record, he said Tinubu inherited a weak economy. “When President Bola Ahmed Tinubu assumed the mantle of leadership in this country, what we had in our foreign reserves was a country with 3.9 billion dollars, barely enough to import oil for one month. And our Ways and Means expenditure was over N27 trillion. “Nigeria was on the road to Caracas. The economy was teetering on the brink of collapse. He literally saved the nation,” Shettima said. He added that “for the first time in nearly 18 years, our foreign reserves are in the neighbourhood of 58.9 billion dollars. He assured that the North has nothing to fear about a Tinubu second term. “For the North, we have absolutely nothing to fear in a Tinubu second term. He has the North at heart,” he said. National Chairman of the APC, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, moved a motion at the event for the President’s return and asked the audience to affirm it. “Today is a time for us to renew a mandate that was largely supported by the North, and the North again will largely support the return of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for a second term,” Yilwatda said. He cited the President’s projects in the region, including the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano and Kano-Maiduguri roads. “Those two roads alone are over 900 kilometres, more than the 700 kilometres of Lagos Road,” he said. The Director General of A4A and former Jigawa State governor, Muhammad Badaru Abubakar, said the new campaign headquarters is at No. 4 Port Harcourt Street, Area 11, Garki, Abuja, and described it as “the biggest campaign office anywhere in the country.” “Let it be understood that this building is more than just a campaign office. It is a message. It says that Arewa is serious,” Badaru said. He said the group would run “a campaign that is disciplined, peaceful and issue-based,” taking its message to markets, farms, campuses, mosques and churches. items.title: Parlement : Ahmed El Abadi succède à Hamouni à la tête du groupe parlementaire du PPS
items.description: Le député Ahmed El Abadi a été désigné, vendredi 16 octobre, président du groupe parlementaire du Parti du progrès et du socialisme (PPS) à la Chambre des représentants, en remplacement de Rachid Hamouni, nommé ministre délégué chargé de l’Inclusion sociale au sein du gouvernement dirigé par Fatima Zahra El Mansouri. Ce changement intervient quelques heures après la nomination des membres du nouvel exécutif par le roi Mohammed VI, au palais royal de Rabat. L’annonce a été faite sur la page officielle du PPS sur Facebook. Le parti y a adressé ses félicitations à Ahmed El Abadi, lui souhaitant de réussir dans ses nouvelles fonctions, au service de l’intérêt général et dans la défense des causes du pays et des citoyens au Parlement. Cette désignation a été précédée d’une réunion du groupe parlementaire, organisée vendredi soir. Les députés du parti y ont examiné les modalités de la prochaine étape et la répartition des responsabilités avant de porter leur choix sur Ahmed El Abadi. Ce dernier dispose déjà d’une expérience parlementaire au sein du PPS. Élu dans la circonscription de Taza pour la législature 2021-2026, il a été reconduit lors des élections législatives du 23 septembre dernier. Il préside également le conseil communal de Galdamane, dans la province de Taza. Au cours de son précédent mandat, Ahmed El Abadi a occupé les fonctions de premier vice-président de la commission des finances et du développement économique de la Chambre des représentants. Il a notamment participé à l’examen de plusieurs textes législatifs, en particulier les projets de loi de finances, et adressé des questions parlementaires sur des enjeux sociaux, économiques et de développement. Trois portefeuilles ministériels pour le PPS La nomination d’Ahmed El Abadi s’inscrit dans une nouvelle configuration politique pour le parti du Livre, qui passe de l’opposition à la majorité gouvernementale. Le PPS a rejoint la coalition quadripartite conduite par Fatima Zahra El Mansouri, aux côtés du Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM), de l’Istiqlal et de l’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP). Cette participation à l’exécutif se traduit par l’attribution de trois portefeuilles ministériels au parti. Nabil Benabdallah a été nommé ministre de l’Éducation nationale, du Préscolaire, de la Formation professionnelle et de la Qualification. Charafat Afailal s’est vu confier le ministère de l’Énergie, des Mines et du Développement durable. Rachid Hamouni, quant à lui, a rejoint le gouvernement en qualité de ministre délégué auprès de la ministre de la Famille, du Développement social et de l’Égalité, chargé de l’Inclusion sociale. Le départ de Rachid Hamouni vers l’exécutif ouvre ainsi une nouvelle séquence pour le groupe parlementaire du PPS. À la tête de celui-ci, Ahmed El Abadi devra coordonner les positions des députés du parti, assurer le suivi des initiatives gouvernementales et participer à l’examen des projets de loi soumis au Parlement. Cette réorganisation intervient alors que le PPS doit désormais articuler son travail législatif avec sa participation à la majorité, dans un contexte où ses représentants sont appelés à contribuer à la fois à l’action gouvernementale et au débat parlementaire. items.title: EC must command public confidence regardless of which party is in power – Victoria Bright
items.description: Private legal practitioner Victoria Bright has called for consistency in the appointment of Electoral Commission (EC) officials, stressing that the Commission must command public confidence regardless of which political party is in power. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 17, she said the appointment of the two new Deputy Chairpersons of the EC must be assessed against consistent standards of constitutional legality, professional suitability and public confidence in their independence. “I think we must approach this issue with a consistent principle. And that principle is that the Electoral Commission must command public confidence, regardless of which party is in government,” she said. Ms Bright cautioned against changing the standards applied to appointments whenever political power changes hands, arguing that the credibility of the electoral body depends not only on the legality of its appointments but also on whether Ghanaians have confidence in its impartiality. She identified three key questions that should guide the assessment of the appointments: whether the constitutional requirements had been met, whether the appointees were suitable for their respective positions, and whether the process provided citizens with reasonable grounds to trust their independence. According to her, these questions are related but must be considered separately. She noted that the 1992 Constitution empowers the President to appoint Electoral Commissioners on the advice of the Council of State, while also protecting the Commission from external direction or control in the performance of its functions. Although she acknowledged that the appointments were not unconstitutional, she said concerns remained about their implications for public confidence in the institution. “The appointments are not unconstitutional, but they do cause concern,” she said. Ms Bright argued that, for an institution as sensitive as the EC, the perception of independence was almost as important as independence itself. She said the central issue was not simply whether the appointments were lawful, but whether they inspired confidence in the neutrality of the Commission across the political divide. Addressing the appointment of Emelia Afi Agbenyo, Ms Bright said concerns about her perceived political affiliations were relevant to the wider discussion about public confidence in the EC. She argued that her reported close association with the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) provided a basis for citizens to question how the appointing authorities had considered the potential implications for perceptions of impartiality. However, Ms Bright stressed that Agbenyo’s qualifications and professional experience deserved fair consideration, adding that competence alone did not automatically resolve questions about independence. “For me, her qualifications and professional experience do deserve fair consideration. But both competence and independence are necessary for this kind of appointment. And evidence of one does not automatically answer questions about the other,” she said. On the appointment of Dr Joseph Kweku Asamoah, she acknowledged that his previous experience within the EC was relevant to his new role. NPP and NDC challenged to maintain consistency Ms Bright also recalled the controversy surrounding appointments to the EC under former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, including the appointment of Chairperson Jean Mensa, who is allegedly related to the former First Lady, Rebecca Akufo-Addo. She said those appointments attracted objections from civil society organisations, including the Coalition of Domestic Election Observers (CODEO), as well as criticism from the NDC, which was then in opposition. In her view, the history of those disagreements meant that both the NPP and the NDC had questions of consistency to answer over their positions on appointments to the electoral body. For the NPP, she said the question was why concerns about partisan associations should carry decisive weight under the current administration when similar concerns were resisted while the party was in government. For the NDC, she questioned how its own appointments measured up to the standards it had demanded when it was in opposition. Ms Bright maintained that political parties should uphold the principles they advocated while in opposition once they assumed office. She cautioned that controversial appointments made by previous administrations should not become a justification for repeating similar controversies. “Earlier controversial appointments cannot become a standing justification for further controversial appointments. We can’t keep going on and on,” she said. Bright questions argument about balancing EC composition The private legal practitioner also expressed concern about the reported explanation from the government side that the appointments were intended to rebalance the composition of the EC. She said such an argument would be troubling if the balance being discussed referred to partisan representation within the Commission. According to her, the EC should not be viewed as a body made up of representatives of competing political interests whose appointments are intended to counterbalance one another. Ms Bright warned that such an approach could undermine the Commission’s role as an impartial arbiter of the electoral process. She maintained that the priority should be to protect the independence and credibility of the institution rather than to create a perception that its composition reflects a political contest between the governing party and the opposition. Her comments come after President John Dramani Mahama swore in Dr Asamoah and Ms Agbenyo as Deputy Chairpersons of the EC on October 16.

items.title: Nigeria awaits 10 attack helicopters, UAVs — Defence Minister
items.description: EU pledges €20m defence support to Nigerian military By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — Nigeria is expecting the delivery of 10 attack helicopters, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and other military equipment to strengthen its capacity to tackle emerging security threats, the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (retd.), has said. Musa disclosed this when he received the European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), Gautier Mignot, and his delegation at Ship House, Abuja. The meeting focused on bilateral defence agreements, including a review of security cooperation between Nigeria and the EU, as well as a proposed €20 million assistance package for the Armed Forces of Nigeria under the European Peace Facility. In a statement by Leah Katung-Babatunde, Special Assistant on Media to the Minister, Mignot commended Nigeria’s defence leadership and invited Musa to a meeting of defence ministers in Brussels later in the year. The minister said the shrinking of the Lake Chad Basin, on which more than 50 million people depend, remained a potential source of instability. He added that denying terrorists access to their strongholds on islands in Lake Chad remained a key operational priority for the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF). Musa thanked the EU for its continued support for Nigeria and assured the ambassador of President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to protecting lives and property and promoting national development. He said relative peace was gradually returning to parts of the country through the efforts of the Armed Forces and other security agencies. However, he acknowledged that kidnapping along major highways and attacks on isolated communities persisted, adding that security agencies were working to address the threats. On the Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration (DDR) programme, the minister stressed that its implementation should prioritise victims of the conflict, including affected military personnel. Mignot disclosed that an EU technical delegation would visit Abuja in November to agree on the details for delivering the proposed assistance. He also commended a recent conference of former and serving MNJTF force commanders, which was attended by representatives of the African Union and the Lake Chad Basin Commission. items.title: Hydrocarbures : l’Algérie mobilise 71,6 milliards $ d’investissements à l’horizon 2030
items.description: L’Algérie a lancé des investissements massifs de 71,6 milliards de dollars pour augmenter sa production d’hydrocarbures à l’horizon 2030. Ce montant a été dévoilé par le ministre des Hydrocarbures, Mohamed Arkab, ce samedi 17 octobre, devant la Commission des finances et du budget de l’APN lors de la présentation du bilan de son secteur et du Projet de loi de finances 2027 . L’Algérie s’est fixée deux objectifs majeurs dans le domaine du pétrole et gaz . Le premier est d’augmenter la production primaire d'hydrocarbures à « environ 201 millions de tonnes équivalent pétrole (tep) d'ici 2030 », a précisé le ministre. La production algérienne d’hydrocarbures devrait atteindre 193 millions TEP en 2026, selon les prévisions de M. Arkab. Le second est « d’accroître le taux de transformation et de valorisation des hydrocarbures » en Algérie pour « dépasser 50 % de la production primaire, contre environ 30 % actuellement », a détaillé M. Arkab. Algérie : 13 milliards de dollars d’investissements dans la pétrochimie à l’horizon 2030 Pour atteindre ces deux objectifs, l’Algérie a réservé une « enveloppe d'investissement estimée à environ 71,6 milliards de dollars » pour le développement du secteur des hydrocarbures, dont « 52 milliards de dollars destinés aux activités en amont et environ 13 milliards de dollars aux projets de raffinage et de pétrochimie », a développé le ministre. Parmi les principaux projets pétrochimiques lancés par l’Algérie et qui sont en cours de réalisation figurent la raffinerie de Hassi Messaoud, une unité de production de Méthyl Tert-Butyl Ether (MTBE), un complexe de production de polypropylène à Arzew, un projet similaire en Turquie, ainsi qu'une unité de production d'Alkyl Benzène linéaire à Skikda. Le ministre a fait état de la hausse de la demande européenne en gaz algérien ainsi que le renouvellement et la signature de contrats d'approvisionnement à long terme avec plusieurs partenaires, dont l'Italie, l'Espagne, la Slovénie, la Tchéquie et l'Allemagne. items.title: PSG fight back to beat Strasbourg after Dembele penalty miss
items.description: Ousmane Dembele missed a penalty but later scored as Paris Saint-Germain produced a fightback to win 3-1 away at Strasbourg on Saturday and go to the top of the French Ligue 1 table. PSG were trailing to an early goal by United States star Giovanni Reyna for Strasbourg at the Stade de la Meinau, and last year’s Ballon d’Or winner Dembele then put a penalty wide in the 72nd minute. But Dembele made amends in style, first by setting up Illia Zabarnyi to equalise in the 78th minute and then by putting the reigning French and European champions ahead with five minutes to go. He then played a part in setting up Desire Doue for PSG’s third in stoppage time, as Luis Enrique’s men made it four straight Ligue 1 wins, and six on the bounce including the Champions League. After failing to win any of their first three domestic league matches this season, PSG are up to 14 points from seven games and are therefore top of the standings on goals scored from Monaco, before the principality club visit Lorient on Sunday. Lille, Rennes, Paris FC and Lyon all have the opportunity to go back above PSG in the table over the weekend. This game, one of PSG’s toughest domestic tests of the season, fell awkwardly just three days after their 4-2 Champions League victory at Manchester City and three days before they host Barcelona. True to form, Luis Enrique therefore made sweeping changes with eight in total from the City game. Dembele was one of those relegated to the bench here with an eye on the upcoming meeting with Barcelona, his former side. Strasbourg sought to take advantage and went in front on 17 minutes when Reyna received a Gessime Yassine pass just inside the area, turned and beat Matvey Safonov low at the goalkeeper’s near post. The visitors were grateful to Safonov for a superb save low down to deny Conrad Harder just after half-time, before Luis Enrique sent on some of the cavalry, including Dembele and Doue. They won a penalty after a VAR check confirmed that a Doue shot had hit the arm of Pape Demba Diop, but Dembele — who scored a penalty in May’s Champions League final win over Arsenal — put his spot-kick wide. However, Dembele crossed from the right for Ukraine defender Zabarnyi to equalise with a cushioned close-range finish, and then controlled on the edge of the box before firing in to make it 2-1. That was his first Ligue 1 goal this season to go with three in the Champions League, and Dembele — who is nominated again for this year’s Ballon d’Or — then brought down a long Safonov kick before finding Ferran Torres who set up Doue to seal the win. Lille are looking to bounce back from a 3-0 Champions League loss at Arsenal when they entertain Brest later, knowing a win will take them to the summit. items.title: NDC must dissociate itself from Obuasi SHTS head over sexual abuse allegations – Vicky Bright
items.description: International corporate lawyer Victoria Bright has urged the National Democratic Congress (NDC) to dissociate itself from the head of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), who is reportedly seeking political office, amid sexual abuse allegations against him. She said anyone facing such serious allegations should not be given greater political influence while the matter remains under scrutiny, stressing the need to protect students and establish the facts through a fair investigation. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 17, Ms Bright questioned why the headmaster would seek political office amid the allegations. “This is exactly the problem with our country. Why should someone like that be contesting for a political post? It is something that defies all logic and all reasoning. I do not understand,” she said. Read also: Obuasi SHTS head accused of sexually abusing students is NDC Juaben secretary seeking chairmanship Ms Bright said the governing party should distance itself from the individual, saying that people facing serious allegations of abuse should not be placed in positions that could increase their power or influence. “And if I were part of the governing party, I would disassociate myself from someone like that. These are not the kind of people who should be given more power. They should not be empowered to carry on perpetrating these kinds of acts,” she said. Her comments come amid public concern over the sexual abuse allegations involving the head of Obuasi SHTS. Ms Bright said the response to the allegations should focus on protecting students, establishing the facts and holding anyone found responsible accountable. She said that the allegations must be investigated fairly, with the evidence guiding any decisions on responsibility. “The measure of our response will be whether students are protected, whether the allegations are fairly investigated, and whether responsibility is established wherever the evidence leads,” she said. Describing the allegations as a serious breach of trust, the lawyer called for a thorough investigation into the headmaster’s conduct. She also said the need to establish what other people who may have had knowledge of the alleged incidents did about them. “The key question for me is what each responsible person knew, when they knew it, and what they did next,” she said. Ms Bright called for the matter to be treated with the seriousness it deserved, given the potential risks to students and the responsibility of school authorities to protect them. She said the headmaster should face prosecution and imprisonment if an investigation established his guilt. “It’s a total abuse of trust, and he must be fully investigated and jailed if he’s found to be culpable,” she said. This comes after JoyNews investigative correspondent Manasseh Azure Awuni said the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School in the Ashanti Region, who has been suspended over sexual abuse allegations against female students, is a serving constituency secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and an aspirant for the chairmanship position. According to him, the headmaster intends to contest the chairmanship at the party’s constituency delegates’ conference, expected before the end of the year.

items.title: Trump deals with Putin, so why should Ghana fear BRICS? – Ablakwa asks
items.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has defended Ghana’s pursuit of BRICS membership, arguing that the United States’ own dealings with Russia demonstrate the importance of pursuing national interests. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 17, 2026, Mr Ablakwa cited President Donald Trump’s recent diesel agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to challenge warnings that Ghana’s engagement with the bloc could attract American sanctions. He argued that Ghana should not be discouraged from building relations with BRICS countries while Washington continued to pursue economic agreements with those same nations. Mr Ablakwa said that while critics were urging Ghana to fear Mr Trump’s influence, the US President was making strategic decisions to advance American interests. “If we really analyse this, President Trump has not stopped dealing with these BRICS countries. He (Donald Trump) has just got into a deal with Russia, President Putin, for diesel as his midterm elections approach, and President Zelensky (Ukrainian President) is furious,” “So we are being told that because of threats from President Trump, our foreign policies should be determined by threats that other countries may be putting out when those same countries are themselves being strategic, being smart, and they are dealing with the countries that you are afraid to deal with,” he argued. Read Also: Ghana risks 10% to 100% tariffs on exports to US under Trump’s threats as it moves to join BRICS He also pointed to economic ties between China and the United States as evidence that cooperation could continue despite political differences. “Indeed, China remains the biggest creditor to the US.” The Minister linked Ghana’s BRICS ambitions to the vision of the country’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, presenting the move as consistent with his pursuit of international solidarity and economic independence. His comments followed concerns, particularly from the opposition New Patriotic Party, about the possible implications of closer engagement with the bloc for Ghana’s relations with Washington. On October 6, Mr Ablakwa announced that Cabinet had approved Ghana’s decision to formally apply to join BRICS, saying the move would diversify international partnerships and create opportunities for trade, investment and economic cooperation. The Trump–Putin agreement cited by the Minister was announced on October 9 following a telephone conversation between the two leaders. According to Reuters, Mr Trump said Russia would supply more than 300,000 metric tonnes of diesel to US and global markets as part of efforts to reduce fuel prices. The arrangement involved easing sanctions on Russian diesel exports. It drew criticism from Ukraine and US lawmakers concerned that the additional revenue could support Moscow’s war effort.

items.title: Asking Agbenyo to resign will mean everyone else at EC must leave – Vicky Bright
items.description: Private legal practitioner Victoria Bright has described calls for newly appointed Electoral Commission (EC) Deputy Chairperson Emelia Affi Agbenyo to resign as excessive, arguing that applying the same standard to other commissioners could require the entire Commission to step down. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 17, Ms Bright said the focus should be on improving the appointment process to ensure that the EC commands public confidence, rather than singling out one appointee for resignation. Her comments follow a call by the Coalition of Domestic Election Observers (CODEO) for Ms Agbenyo to resign over concerns about her past political activities and their potential impact on public confidence in the Commission’s independence and impartiality. Ms Bright argued that demanding Ms Agbenyo’s resignation while allowing other commissioners with perceived political affiliations to remain in office would amount to applying different standards to individuals serving on the same institution. “I think that’s a step too far. If they are saying that, then everybody there should resign, from the EC Chair down. The EC Chair, we know, has a very strong family and political affiliation with the opposition party,” she said. She added that other members of the Commission also had political affiliations, questioning why one individual should be singled out for resignation while others remained in office. “So you can’t pick and choose. You can’t choose one and say resign, and this one stays and all of that. We are where we are,” she said. READ ALSO: CODEO calls for Emelia Agbnyo’s resignation over partisan ties Ms Bright said the focus should instead be on addressing the weaknesses in the process for appointing members of the EC to prevent similar controversies in the future. She maintained that previous administrations had made appointments that attracted criticism over perceived political affiliations, adding that the country needed to move beyond the recurring disagreements and consider the kind of electoral management body it wanted to establish. She argued that the debate should not be limited to whether appointments made by one administration were acceptable while those made by another were not. According to her, successive governments had appointed individuals perceived to be aligned with their respective political parties, making it necessary to reconsider the process rather than continue the cycle. “Every party that has come into power has appointed its own people. So for me, we should now look beyond that and ask ourselves a very, very important question. The test for me is what kind of Electoral Commission that we want to build,” she said. EC must inspire confidence across political divide Ms Bright said the ultimate test should be whether the Commission could earn the trust of both major political parties and the wider Ghanaian public, particularly when its decisions did not favour their interests. She stressed that improving the appointment process was necessary to establish an electoral body whose independence and impartiality would be accepted across the political divide. “The test for me is whether we are building an Electoral Commission that both parties and the wider public, Ghanaians, can trust when decisions go against them,” she said.

items.title: Akosua Manu calls for a proper protection framework for sexually abused children
items.description: Adviser on Gender and Social Protection to former Vice-President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, Akosua Manu, has called for a proper national child protection framework to safeguard pupils who suffer sexual abuse in schools. She said Ghana needs a clear system through which children can report abuse, receive protection and seek justice without fear of exposure or intimidation. Speaking on JoyNews ’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 17, during a discussion on sexual abuse allegations involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Ms Manu said the current arrangements did not adequately protect children who reported such cases. “So, fundamentally, there’s no protection for these girls, for these children in the schools,” she said. She said that a national framework should establish safe and confidential reporting channels to ensure that children are protected and their concerns handled with the seriousness they deserve. “I would think to cure the problem, there should be a framework, a national protection framework, safeguarding these girls, where reports of such cases go to, that there should be a channel where you report to, where you get protected, where your name or where your form or whatever is hidden,” she said. Ms Manu said that the system must put the welfare of the child first, particularly when the alleged abuse involves someone in a position of authority within a school. “It should be such that the child is prioritised,” she added. Ms Manu also raised concerns about situations in which children are expected to report abuse to the same school authorities they accuse of misconduct. She said such arrangements could discourage victims from speaking out, especially when they fear that their complaints may not be handled fairly. “But I believe fundamentally a child should not have to seek justice from the same authorities that they’re accusing of abuse,” she said. Ms Manu referred to a News card shared by JoyNews which stated that six headteachers had allegedly sexually assaulted girls in their schools since 2025. She said the reported cases raised serious concerns about the effectiveness of existing measures to protect pupils and called for urgent policy action. “You can imagine the number of girls that have gone through this,” she said. “And you can imagine the ones that are under-reported. It is a national crisis,” she added, referring to the reported cases. The allegations against the Obuasi SHTS headmaster have not, in the details provided, been established as proven findings. Ms Manu’s call for reforms centres on ensuring that allegations of abuse are reported safely and investigated properly, while protecting children from further harm. She called for a policy that would make children feel comfortable reporting abuse and confident that their complaints would be handled appropriately. “We need to put a policy in place that makes kids comfortable,” she said. “The last place a child should not feel safe should not be a school. At least, at the very least, from home to school, they should feel safe,” she added.

items.title: Indian airlines barred from using Pakistani airspace until Nov 24 as ban extended
items.description: Pakistan has extended its airspace ban for Indian aircraft for another month, until Nov 24, according to a Notice to Airmen (Notam) issued by the Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA). The previous extension of the ban was set to expire on Oct 24. “Pakistan airspace not available for Indian registered aircraft and aircraft operated/owned or leased by Indian airlines/operators, including military flights,” the Notam said. According to the notice, the extension came into effect at 7:45pm on Saturday and will remain until 04:59am on Nov 24, 2026. The country’s airspace is divided into two flight information regions (FIRs) — Karachi and Lahore, according to a Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority (PCAA) document from 2022. Saturday’s Notam applies to both the Karachi (OPKR) and Lahore (OPLR) FIRs. India and Pakistan closed their airspaces to each other’s airlines in late April 2025, when tensions between them escalated in the wake of a deadly attack in India-occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam. On April 24, Pakistan’s top brass had announced a series of measures , including the closure of its airspace to all India-owned or Indian-operated airlines with immediate effect, as it retaliated against New Delhi’s slew of aggressive measures against the country. New Delhi, without evidence, had alleged that Islamabad backed the Pahalgam attack. However, Pakistan had strongly denied any involvement and offered a neutral probe . The nuclear powers had the fiercest air battle in May, in which Pakistan said it downed seven Indian fighter jets. Since then, Pakistan has extended the airspace ban several times, forcing Indian carriers to use longer and costlier routes. For Air India, the country’s only carrier with a major international network, fuel costs rose by as much as 29 per cent and journey times by up to three hours on some long-haul routes, according to a document submitted to Indian officials last October. The airline, owned by Tata Group and Singapore Airlines, estimated the Pakistan airspace closure’s impact on its profit before tax at $455 million annually — a significant amount given its fiscal 2024-25 loss stood at $439m.

items.title: Remi Tinubu urges more opportunities for vulnerable families
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — First Lady Oluremi Tinubu has called for sustained efforts to expand access to education, healthcare, skills acquisition, decent livelihoods and economic opportunities, particularly for vulnerable families, as Nigeria joins the world to mark the 2026 International Day for the Eradication of Poverty. In a message issued on Saturday, Tinubu said the occasion, observed under the theme “United for Peace and Human Rights,” highlighted the collective responsibility to build a society where everyone could live with dignity and hope. “The International Day for the Eradication of Poverty 2026, with the theme ‘United for Peace and Human Rights,’ reminds us of our collective responsibility to build a society where every person can live with dignity and hope, access meaningful opportunities, and thrive to realise their full potential,” she said. The First Lady stressed that efforts to tackle poverty must prioritise vulnerable households and create conditions that enable people to improve their living standards. “We must continue expanding access to education, healthcare, skills, decent livelihoods, and economic opportunities, especially for vulnerable families,” she said. She added that compassion, effective interventions and sustained collaboration were essential to helping individuals and families escape poverty. “Through compassion, effective interventions, and sustained collaboration, we can create pathways out of poverty and towards shared prosperity,” she said. Tinubu wished Nigerians a happy International Day for the Eradication of Poverty. The day is observed annually on October 17. According to the United Nations, the theme for 2026–2028 is “United for Peace and Human Rights”, while the focus for this year is “Safe Homes for All”. items.title: Nigeria’s economy needs continuation of Tinubu’s reforms – Wike
items.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says Nigeria’s full economic recovery depends entirely on sustaining the bold reform policies initiated by President Bola Tinubu. Wike said this on Saturday, at the Rainbow Coalition’s stakeholders’ consultation in Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area of Rivers. He said that only the continuation of the current administration’s economic direction could permanently pull the country back from the brink of collapse. He noted that the hard economic choices being implemented presently were necessary remedies to salvage a system that was virtually “dead” when Tinubu took office. “Only the continuation of the economic reforms initiated by the Tinubu government can bring this country back from the economic comatose it was in before this present administration took over,” he said. He said that the presidential candidate of the Africa Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Abubakar Atiku and his vice, Rotimi Amaechi, had nothing to offer to Nigerians. The minister urged residents of the state not to surrender the country’s progress to “career politicians” and “political opportunists” whom he likened to “chronic pool betters” who repeatedly gamble with public trust. According to him, supporting politicians who have made decades-long pursuits for power would mean diverting national funds to recoup lost campaign expenses rather than consolidating economic gains. Wike further said that the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, would not make any meaningful difference if elected, stressing that Tinubu was the person who had shown true commitment. Reaffirming that leadership must be judged by past governance records, the former Rivers governor challenged his predecessor to account for major capital allocations in Rivers. Explaining the political strategy behind the cross-party Rainbow Coalition movement, he said that delivering economic recovery required total alignment between the executive and the national assembly. He urged voters to support Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates vying for the Senate and House of Representatives seats in the area to ensure legislative cooperation for the president’s economic policy agenda. He also called on party leaders and community mobilisers to prepare for an overwhelming turnout on election day. “I want total mobilisation on Jan. 16, 2027. Everybody must be mobilised. Make sure we vote and win decisively to protect our collective future,” he said. In his remarks, the Executive Chairman of the council, Dr Chukwu Shedrack, commended Wike for his historic development projects in the council, including road construction, hospital upgrades, and human capital investments. Shedrack highlighted several local governance achievements which he said aligned with the FCT minister’s leadership model. Reaffirming the council’s political commitment to the Tinubu administration’s economic recovery drive, he pledged a complete block vote for the APC across all elective positions come 2027. “We are fully mobilised, ward by ward and unit by unit. Come the 2027 general elections, our people will deliver 100 per cent. From president to national assembly and house of assembly, no vote will drop,” Shedrack assured. (NAN) The post Nigeria’s economy needs continuation of Tinubu’s reforms – Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Looting, blazes and clashes in France amid nationwide protests
items.description: Police and protesters clashed violently in Paris and other French cities on Saturday on the sidelines of nationwide marches against soaring inflation, with one demonstrator’s hand blown off, multiple blazes set, and looters breaking into dozens of stores to strip them bare. With just months to go before the two-round elections in April and May to choose Macron’s successor, the demonstrations follow weeks of high-school student blockades demanding better learning conditions. Macron and his government were criticised by many of the demonstrators, who numbered 500,000 across the country, according to the CGT union. Authorities did not immediately give their estimate of the numbers. Police used tear gas and water cannon against masked protesters in Paris and other cities who were throwing projectiles and aiming fireworks. Several parked cars were torched in the capital, and more than 130 arrests were made. In the southern city of Saint-Etienne, a male protester had his hand blown off by a police crowd-control grenade, a police source told AFP . His maiming came after a 15-year-old lost his hand on October 5 to a police stun grenade during another protest in the city of Lens. Protesters stand amid tear gas smoke as clashes erupt ahead of a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, at Place de la Republique in Paris, France on October 17, 2026. — AFP The protests geared up with a handful of gatherings nationwide on Saturday morning, AFP reporters said. In Lyon, protesters set ablaze a tourist office in the city centre, and smashed their way into town halls in the cities of Marseille and Lille, where they vandalised the premises before leaving. Dozens of shops were looted, including many in Marseille, among them a Hermes boutique, an Apple store in Lille, several shops in Nice and at least one mobile phone outlet in Paris, AFP journalists saw. A crowd of more than 300 protesters tried to move up Paris’s Champs-Elysees, home to flagship luxury stores. As police firing tear gas blocked their way, they yelled, “All cops are bastards”. In the western city of Rennes, around 20 people set up a barricade using trash bins and large pallets on the outskirts of a shopping mall. Christophe, a 47-year-old carpenter and former Yellow Vest protester who did not give his surname, said he was indignant after seeing what he viewed as police brutality against teenagers in recent weeks. “We’ve reached the point where the repression is targeting our own children,” he told AFP . A French national police officer fires tear gas during clashes prior to the start of a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, in Marseille, southern France on October 17, 2026. — AFP ‘Macron, resign’ The looting and confrontations with police were being carried out by masked youths on the sidelines of marches that were largely peaceful and which attracted people of all ages, including families with children. Paris mayor Emmanuel Gregoire stressed that “the overwhelming majority of demonstrators” wanted to “march calmly”, but “acts of vandalism” were tarnishing their protest. In Paris, tens of thousands marched across the east and north of the city in one major march, some shouting “Everyone hates the police” and “Macron, resign”. Protesters wearing yellow vests face police as clashes erupt ahead of a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, at Place de la Republique in Paris, France on October 17, 2026. — AFP One demonstrator, Jules Petrichor, 47, who had brought his son, said: “There was a good atmosphere and then suddenly they (the police) started gassing us, even though nothing was happening. Naturally that worsened things and the hot-heads got hot-headed.” Another protester who gave his first name as Louis, 19, complained that police were trigger-happy any time there was a demonstration. “We can’t protest any more, it’s frightening,” he said. The country’s Yellow Vest movement, which eight years ago staged street protests against Macron’s government over planned fuel tax hikes, has called Saturday’s “yellow and youth” demonstrations. It has appealed to teachers and students, workers, pensioners and farmers to take part in the protests on the first day of half-term holidays. The principal grievance was the cost of living — pushed up in part by the war in the Middle East — that has helped send inflation soaring in Europe as elsewhere. But there were other issues too. A protestor with a gas mask holds a French flag in front of a fire at the Boulevard des Capucines during a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, in Paris, France on October 17, 2026. — AFP High school student Kamil Alahyan, 18, said he was protesting “for so many reasons — the elections coming up in 2027, politicians who lie, the ultra-rich who’ve been taking more and more wealth over the past 10 years”. “For years we’ve had climate, economy and equality problems but the government is not doing anything about it,” said Agnes, a 50-year-old actor who did not give her second name. Anae, a 24-year-old student who did not give her surname, said she was protesting because she did not have a “sustainable future”. “Our planet’s burning. And we’ve got a government that doesn’t give a toss,” she said. Le Pen blames ‘rioters’ Opposition politicians vying to succeed Macron have seized upon the protests. Far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, who has sided with the police, said on X: “Looting, pillaging, attacking police — rioters have once again sullied the October 17 demonstrations over the cost of living.” She claimed that the protesters’ demands had been “hijacked by the far left”. Her far-left rival Jean-Luc Melenchon, insisted early Saturday that “everything is passing off peacefully”, while accusing television news of “flooding us with images of violence in dozens of cities”. Several protesters sought to draw parallels with the French Revolution of 1789. “It’s the Revolution — we’re taking the Bastille!” some shouted in Marseille during the forced entry of the mayor’s offices. In the western city of La Rochelle, marchers streamed behind a placard reading: “Revolution or death.” And in the southern city of Montpellier, a giant blue sign reading “The people will win” was unfurled above a central square. “The government is trembling and it’s right to tremble because when the French people are angry, they never let up,” Ryad Rani, the head of the LSU high school student representative body, told journalists in Paris.

items.title: Troops rescue 27 abducted residents in Katsina Forest
items.description: By Fauziyya Lawal, Katsina KATSINA — Troops of the Nigerian Army, working with local hunters and the Community Watch Corps, have rescued 27 residents abducted by armed bandits during an attack on Gamji village in Sabuwa Local Government Area of Katsina State. The attack, which occurred on Friday, also claimed the life of a 70-year-old resident, Alhaji Saleh Kasim, while six cows were reportedly rustled. The Katsina State Ministry of Internal Security and Home Affairs disclosed this in a statement issued on Saturday, October 17, 2026. According to the statement, signed by the state Commissioner for Internal Security and Home Affairs, Dr Nasir Mu’azu, about 40 armed bandits, reportedly led by a gang leader identified as Kachalla Alhaji Bawa Kabir, invaded the community in the early hours of October 16 on 20 motorcycles. The attackers abducted 27 residents, comprising mainly women, children and elderly people, and killed Kasim during the raid. The ministry said security forces launched a coordinated operation after receiving intelligence about the attack. Troops of the 17 Brigade mobilised alongside local hunters and members of the Community Watch Corps to pursue the fleeing attackers and secure the release of the victims. The joint security team reportedly blocked escape routes towards the Madaci forest enclave to prevent the bandits from moving the abducted residents deeper into the forest. The operation culminated at about 6pm on Friday when troops engaged the suspected bandits at Tashar Bawa forest and rescued all 27 victims, according to the statement. The rescued residents were subsequently taken to the Machika Military Forward Operating Base for medical attention and other necessary care. The ministry added that joint security teams had commenced clearance operations to track down suspected members of the gang who escaped the encounter. The operations are also aimed at preventing possible reprisal attacks and protecting Gamji and neighbouring communities from further threats. Mu’azu commended the troops of the 17 Brigade, local hunters and the Community Watch Corps for their prompt response, courage and cooperation, which he said contributed to the successful rescue. He reaffirmed the commitment of the Katsina State Government, under Governor Dikko Umaru Radda, to protecting lives and property and intensifying security operations in communities affected by criminal activities.
